literal_gloss: the concealed/invisible beings (etymological gloss is interpretive)
definition: A Qur'anic category of morally addressed nonhuman beings; the selected passages include a group who hear revelation and jinn who work for Sulayman by divine permission.
cultural_caution: Do not equate jinn with 'genies,' wish-granters, demons, or a single fantasy species. The term has Qur'anic, theological, literary, regional, and living-context histories that must remain distinguished.

supports: A company of jinn reports hearing a wondrous recitation.
The passage distinguishes those among the jinn who submit from those who deviate.

definition: A Qur'anic designation appearing in the selected Sulayman passage for beings subjected to work, and in the Adam passage for the whispering adversary.
cultural_caution: Do not silently equate shayatin with all jinn, with Iblis alone, or with the taxonomy's Western-derived demon/devil families. The selected text uses distinct terms and later interpretation varies.

supports: Shayatin are described as subjected to dive and perform other work for Sulayman.
The shaytan whispers to Adam in the cited narrative.

definition: In Qur'an 27:39, an ifrit 'of the jinn' offers to bring the throne before Sulayman rises from his place. The passage supplies a designation, not a personal name.
cultural_caution: This term is retained as a source term rather than turned into a character node or a fantasy 'efreet' subtype. Later literary and game uses are separate continuities.

supports: An ifrit of the jinn speaks and offers the stated action, without a personal name.

definition: Qur'an 55:15 states that the jann was created from a marij of fire.
cultural_caution: A translated creation phrase is not an elemental-stat block, damage type, or proof that all later jinn depictions share one body theory.

supports: The jann is stated to have been created from a smokeless/mingled flame of fire.

definition: In the selected Sulayman account, the jinn are said not to know the unseen, a textual limit that cautions against blanket claims of jinn omniscience.
cultural_caution: Al-ghayb is a religious concept, not an interchangeable 'spirit world,' hidden map layer, or divination mechanic.

supports: The jinn are said not to have known the unseen in the cited account.

definition: The phrase qualifies the jinn's work before Sulayman in Qur'an 34:12.
cultural_caution: The cited theological qualification must not be recast as evidence for ordinary conjuration, possession, enslavement, or a reproducible ritual of spirit binding.

supports: The jinn work before Sulayman by his Lord's permission.
